instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines lobbying as "attempting to influence legislative or administrative action by oral or written communication," enumerating only oral and written modes (plus preparation/appearances at hearings).

A "lobbyist" is an individual employed by or contracting with a principal; a "principal" includes any person, association, corporation, LLC, or partnership employing a lobbyist — covering professional contract lobbyists and in-house lobbyists for companies and organizations, but agencies are expressly excluded (per AG opinion and §13.621(2)-(3)).
The definitions section §13.62 does not define "public entity"; it defines "agency," "business entity," etc., but not "public entity."

The statute includes materiality thresholds: principals making expenditures of $500 or less annually may file a verified statement exempting them from licensing/registration/reporting, and an individual whose duties are not exclusively lobbying is a lobbyist only if making communications on at least 5 days per reporting period.

Lobbying covers communications with "any elective state official, agency official or legislative employee," and "legislative action" includes the governor's approval/veto, so the definition covers both legislative and executive officials including the governor.

Targets of lobbying include elective state officials (legislative branch), agency officials (executive/administrative bureaucracy), and legislative employees (staff), covering legislative, executive, and administrative branches.

Lobbying targets include elective state officials and agency officials, and legislative action includes the governor's actions, satisfying coverage of legislators and executive officials including the governor.
Same as above — §13.62(10) covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials and legislative employees, and "legislative action" in §13.62(8) includes gubernatorial action.

Lobbying definition covers oral/written communications with state legislators (elective state officials/legislative employees) and executive officials (agency officials), and includes the governor's approval/veto actions.
Targets include elective state officials (legislative branch), agency officials (executive branch and bureaucracy), and legislative employees (staff).

Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees acting in their official capacity are exempt from registration/licensing/reporting requirements, so they are not required to register as lobbyists.

The statute applies time standards (5-day threshold for non-exclusive lobbyists), expenditure thresholds ($500 in §13.621(5)), and compensation criteria (economic consideration beyond expense reimbursement); and §13.695 separately addresses agency employees whose duties include influencing legislative action.
No definition in §13.62 relies on public charter or special government protection; definitions are based on roles, employment relationships, and activity types.
No definition in §13.62 relies on ownership; "business entity" is defined by profit-operation status not ownership structure.
No definition in §13.62 relies on structure or composition of revenue; the definitions turn on roles and lobbying activity, not revenue composition.
